name: EPP Circle
character: Hexies on the table: lavender, round corners, and a guild that papers, bastes, and talks while the kettle boils.

sections.title: {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: We glue-baste, whipstitch, and fussy-cut. Meetings are {{meeting_info}}.

sections.heading: Sew night
sections.note: Bring a tin of papers, a glue pen, and whatever you are stitching. Needles and thread are on the table.

items.title: Paper packs
items.body: A new shape each month: hexie, jewel, clamshell, or tumbling block. PDFs in the newsletter.

items.title: Fussy-cut bee
items.body: Saturday mornings for people who want to match a print across a seam.

items.title: Finish night
items.body: Once a quarter we pull papers and bind. No new starts that evening.

sections.title: Your first tin is on us
sections.body: New members leave with a hexie pack and the current glue-baste notes.

sections.title: A hand-piecing guild
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Machines stay at home. This room is for paper, thread, and the conversation that happens between stitches.

sections.html:
{{guild_name}} started as four people around a kitchen table with a bag of 1-inch hexies. We still meet {{meeting_info}} in {{city}}. The business meeting is ten minutes. The rest is stitching.

We are not a modern guild and not a Baltimore guild. If you like English paper piecing, you already know how to sit with us.

items.quote: I had a drawer of papers I never pulled. Two sew nights later the drawer is empty and the quilt has a center.
items.author: Diane K.

items.quote: Nobody minds if you talk more than you stitch. The hexies still get done.
items.author: Priya S.

sections.title: This year's papers
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: One shape a month, sized for a 60-inch throw if you keep up, or a cushion if you do not.

items.title: January to April
items.body: 1-inch hexies, then jewels, then a clamshell row. Glue-baste notes in the newsletter.

items.title: May to August
items.body: Tumbling blocks and a fussy-cut floral round. Optional English-paper diamond border.

items.title: September to December
items.body: Pull papers, join sections, and bind at the December finish night.

sections.title: Bees
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Small groups, a shared tin, and a standing night.

items.title: Tuesday tin
items.body: Four to six people, 7 to 9, rotating dining rooms.

items.title: Library bee
items.body: Thursday mornings at the public library. Quiet stitching, no machines.

items.title: Mail bee
items.body: For members who cannot drive at night. A round-robin of papers and leftover prints.

sections.title: Membership
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: One level. Dues cover the hall, the paper packs, and the newsletter.

items.q: Do I need to know English paper piecing already?
items.a: No. The first meeting is a glue-baste demo. Bring fabric scraps if you have them; we have papers.
Not at the monthly meeting. Some bees use a machine to join finished sections. Handwork is the default.

items.title: Monthly programs
items.body: Sample text — replace me: Speakers, trunk shows and demonstrations at every meeting.

items.title: Workshops at member rates
items.body: Hands-on classes with visiting teachers, booked before they open to the public.

items.title: The newsletter
items.body: Meeting reminders, block patterns and what the bees are working on.

items.title: The library
items.body: Books, patterns and templates to borrow at any meeting.

items.title: Show entry
items.body: Enter the annual show, and help hang it.

items.title: The people
items.body: Quilters in Ann Arbor, Michigan who will answer the question you are stuck on.
